principles: Runner command must be explicit and never triggered by normal local lifecycle commands.
Dry-run must be side-effect free: no network mutation and no provider execution.
Fake-provider execution must be bounded by claimed job identity and signed provider events.
Authority receipt/evidence production must not be overclaimed by local status or planning artifacts.
drivers: Preserve local/off usability while adding enforce-only runner behavior.
Reuse B-1123 contract/signing/client primitives instead of inventing a second authority protocol.
Provide mechanical smoke tests for happy, edge, and adversarial verification intents.

options.name: thin-explicit-runner
pros: Allows dry-run and fake-provider smokes without production server dependency
cons: Does not yet integrate real provider CLIs
Requires later receipt-backed evidence story for production classification

options.name: always-on-authority-runner
cons: Risks blocking local users without paid/server authority
Could accidentally trigger provider execution from ordinary lifecycle commands
Harder to test safely in local development

options.name: status-only-placeholder
cons: Does not satisfy job claim/provider event milestones
Leaves no mechanical proof of runner flow

rationale: Choose the explicit once/dry-run runner because it advances real job claim and provider-event mechanics while preserving the local/off safety boundary established in earlier milestones.

preMortem.scenario: Runner is invoked implicitly by a normal lifecycle command
preMortem.trigger: Command wiring shares authority runner side effects with story_advance or verification_evidence_add
preMortem.consequence: Local users unexpectedly contact authority or execute provider jobs
preMortem.mitigation: Keep a dedicated authority_enforce_runner command and add adversarial smoke assertions that normal lifecycle commands do not invoke runner paths

preMortem.scenario: Dry-run mutates authority or executes a provider command
preMortem.trigger: Dry-run reuses live execution branch too late
preMortem.consequence: Users cannot safely inspect planned runner steps
preMortem.mitigation: Model dry-run as a plan projection with spawned:false/providerEvents:[] and fake server asserting no mutation/event endpoints were hit

preMortem.scenario: Provider events are accepted for the wrong job or run
preMortem.trigger: Fake execution omits lease/run/provider identity checks
preMortem.consequence: Evidence could be attached to an unrelated producer/verifier flow
preMortem.mitigation: Bind events to claimed JobSpec/run IDs and add mismatched/unleased rejection tests

preMortem.consequence: Weak evidence can pass despite command failure
preMortem.mitigation: Add failing command smoke that emits failed provider event and returns non-zero runner result
